No GCS bucket is configured in scripts/config.py either, so toCloudStorage isn't available as-is. Real blocker for the GeoTIFF format specifically -- needs either a GCS bucket set up and billing-linked to this GEE project, or a different export target, before GeoTIFF can be offered. Matches MERA_KHET_PROMPT.md's own fallback: ship SHP+PNG+GeoJSON+KML now, mark GeoTIFF 'jald aa raha hai' (coming soon).

benchmarks.label: 5_shpwrite_browser_conversion
benchmarks.method: Real MP village layer (52 districts fetched live from HF, merged: 55,937 villages, 48.9 MB GeoJSON -- matches MERA_KHET_PROMPT.md's own cited example of 'Madhya Pradesh, 55,392 gaon, ~48 MB' almost exactly). Tested @mapbox/shp-write both in Node.js and in a real Chrome tab (ruling out a Node-vs-browser artifact) via its documented zip() API.

10_features.verdict: correct, all features present (plausible byte count)

522_features_one_district_bhopal.verdict: SEVERE DROP -- only 2 of 522 features survived

55937_features_whole_state_mp.verdict: SEVERE DROP -- only 22 of 55937 features survived, confirmed identical in Node and real Chrome

benchmarks.finding: @mapbox/shp-write silently drops the overwhelming majority of features somewhere between 10 and 522 input polygons -- confirmed in both Node.js and a real browser tab, so this is not a test-environment artifact. This is a REAL BLOCKER for the SHP export format at any realistic district/state scale (a single farmer's one polygon, ~1 feature, would likely work fine per the 10-feature result -- the risk is specifically the Location Selector's district/state-level bulk SHP download, not Mera Khet's own single-polygon SHP export). Root cause not fully diagnosed (a known shp-write library limitation at scale is suspected but not confirmed against its GitHub issues). RECOMMENDATION: Mera Khet's own single-polygon SHP download is very likely fine (1 feature, same regime as the working 10-feature test) and can ship. The Location Selector's bulk district/state SHP download must NOT ship using @mapbox/shp-write as-is until this is root-caused or replaced with a different library/approach (e.g. a server-side/Python shapefile writer via a GitHub Action, pre-built once per state rather than generated client-side on demand).
